correctness.rationale: A nilpotent Jacobson radical makes reduction reflect nilpotence; equal-size fibers give the equality of propensities pointwise, not just equality of the means. For a rank-r matrix A, AB maps into W=im A. Its restriction to W is uniform in End(W) by surjectivity of B↦AB|W, and AB is nilpotent exactly when that restriction is. The Fitting-decomposition sum for q^(m²)/|GL_m| telescopes on subtracting the dimension-(m−1) identity, giving q^(m²−m) nilpotents, including the separate trivial m=0 case. Counting image spaces and surjections recovers the rank masses; counting expected kernel elements gives mean 2a−a² for one block. For the convex bound, given block propensity Z, choose an endpoint H∈{a,1} with conditional mean Z; the marginal mass at 1 is a. Independent such choices over the blocks give E[∏H_i | (Z_i)]=∏Z_i. Jensen is strict for every strictly convex function when some block has a positive chance of intermediate rank, since all endpoints are positive and the conditional product is then nonconstant. For n=2 the shadow variance is a(1−a)^3 at a=q^(−2). Its excess over the matrix variance is E[(1−Z)(Z−a)], supported only at rank one and equal to q/(q+1) times the shadow variance. Truncated polynomial factors have the required orders and residue fields. The frozen multiplication-table verifier and output were inspected as finite evidence only; the reasoning checks the general theorem independently of them.

value.rationale: The conditional law retains information the usual nilpotent-product probability loses: equal-order rings with equal scalar probabilities can be distinguished by the entire spread of partner counts, with strict inequality detected already by variance. The equality criterion identifies commutativity of the semisimple quotient, not of the original ring. The exact order-q^4 pair and ratio quantify a natural comparison made for all blocks, rather than a small isolated enumeration.
